title: Part Thirty-Eight: The Missing Election: Who Picks the CEO

sections.brief: Selection and removal in the texts' own words: Moldbug via Land (shares, board, 'hires and fires managers'); Land's gloss (map 'political bribery' into shares, voters 'with appropriate derision', CEO appointment, interest in politics 'semi-criminal', 'No voice, free exit'); Moldbug 2007-08 (hereditary principle, 'without regard to the residents' opinions', 'all exit, no voice'); transition via one victory and a 'qualified administrator' and the 2012 'national CEO'; NYT 2025 ('most important question', no removal mechanism, 'pick one at random' = Fortune 500 CEOs, voting 'pornographic stimulus', 'president of all Americans'); keys only as reviewer's paraphrase; Thiel 2009 and 2022 practice. Figures: compare, flow

How real systems pick and remove rulers, with documented failures: EIC (proprietors elect 24 directors; Parliament's Board of Control 1784; abolished 1858), Rome 193 (Praetorian auction), Venice 1268 (lot against bribery), Saudi 2017 (Allegiance Council 31/34), Kuwait 2006 (parliament removes a sick emir), China (1982 limit, 2018 vote 2,958-2-3), Singapore (party procedure), OpenAI 2023 (board fires CEO, reversed in five days), Palantir founders' voting trust; lesson: removal needs an independent power. Figures: compare, time

Customer, not voter (Fnargland, 'clients', 'customer service function'); who the shareholders are (current holders of influence; formalism's certificate; Próspera council 4+4, Urbit 185/256); exit for those with passports and money (183.2m passports; renunciation fee $2,350 to $450; 1185(b); passport denial; Soviet and Chinese exit controls; Thiel NZ/Malta/Buenos Aires as lawful examples); Hirschman; surplus residents link de6; closing worst-case test for the part. Figures: compare, stats
